```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site
from pdi.tech_value import dashboard

# Bundle the table script into the page instead of loading it from a CDN.
init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

value, meta = site.load("tech-value", "value")
history, hist_meta = site.load("tech-value", "price_history")
coverage, cov_meta = site.load("tech-value", "coverage")
bench, bench_meta = site.load("tech-value", "benchmarks")
version = meta.get("blender_version")

COLUMNS = {
    "model_key": "Model",
    "score_per_dollar": "Score per $",
    "price_usd": "Lowest price (USD)",
    "Retailer": "Cheapest at",
    "median_price_usd": "Median price (USD)",
    "n_retailers": "Stores",
    "Confidence": "Confidence",
    "collected_date": "Price collected",
    "score": "Benchmark score",
    "n_runs": "Benchmark runs",
    "backend": "Backend",
    "n_listings": "Listings",
}
COLUMNS = {
    k: v for k, v in COLUMNS.items()
    if k == "Retailer" or k in value.columns or (k == "Confidence" and "confidence" in value.columns)
}
CONFIDENCE = {"low": "Low: single listing", "normal": "Normal"}


def ranking(kind: str, label: str):
    part = value[value["kind"] == kind] if len(value) else value
    if part.empty:
        return Markdown(site.empty_state(meta, label))
    names = {m["id"]: m["name"] for m in meta.get("sources", [])}
    part = part.assign(
        model_key=part["model_key"].map(dashboard.display_name),
        Retailer=[
            f'<a href="{url}">{names.get(key, key)}</a>' if url else names.get(key, key)
            for key, url in zip(part["retailer"], part["listing_url"])
        ],
    )
    if "confidence" in part.columns:
        part = part.assign(Confidence=part["confidence"].map(CONFIDENCE))
    table = part[list(COLUMNS)].rename(columns=COLUMNS).round(
        {"Score per $": 3, "Benchmark score": 1}
    )
    return show(table, paging=True, pageLength=25, order=[[1, "desc"]], showIndex=False,
                classes="display compact", allow_html=True)
```

## Data coverage and freshness

How many models make it from a benchmark score to a ranked price. The price collectors look up
the `{python} dashboard.config.CRAWLER_MODELS_PER_KIND` most-benchmarked models of each kind every
day; a model is ranked only when a listing is recognised as that model and its price is no more
than `{python} dashboard.config.PRICE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` days old.

```{python}
#| output: asis
html(dashboard.coverage_html(bench, value, history))
html(f"""
<script>window.__vdDefine = window.define; window.define = undefined;</script>
<script src="{plotly_src}" charset="utf-8"></script>
<script>window.define = window.__vdDefine;</script>
<script>{pick_js}</script>
<script>{js}</script>
""")
```

<details class="tv-disclosure"><summary>GPU and CPU ranking tables</summary>


**Score per dollar** is the median [Blender benchmark](https://opendata.blender.org/) score of
a part divided by its cheapest new listing among the US retailers collected. It measures rendering throughput
per dollar and nothing else: not gaming frame rates, not power draw, not noise. Treat a high
value as a reason to look closer, not as a recommendation.

Every price is shown with the retailer it came from and the date this site collected it.
Prices come from one store that allows automated collection and, once a week, from Amazon US
and Best Buy listings supplied by a data provider. Only Amazon listings sold by Amazon.com or
the part's own brand, and Best Buy listings sold by Best Buy itself, are counted, so every
price is for a new part. A cheaper listing may exist elsewhere.

A row marked **Low: single listing** has only one listing behind its price. That is often a
marketplace seller's asking price for a part that is no longer made, so treat its score per
dollar as unreliable. Type "Normal" in the search box to hide those rows.

<details class="tv-disclosure"><summary>Listing coverage</summary>


How much of what is on sale could be matched. A listing has to be recognised as a specific
model, and that model needs enough benchmark runs on the Blender version in use. Unmatched
products are left out of the ranking, never guessed.

```{python}
if coverage.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(cov_meta, "Coverage")))
else:
    display(Markdown(coverage.rename(columns={
        "kind": "Kind", "listings": "Listings collected",
        "listings_recognised": "Recognised as a model", "models_priced": "Distinct models priced",
        "models_with_score": "Models with a benchmark score", "share_with_score": "Share with score",
    }).to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".0%")))
```

</details>

<details class="tv-disclosure"><summary>Benchmark scores without prices</summary>

```{python}
if bench.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(bench_meta, "Benchmark scores")))
else:
    bench_view = bench[["kind", "model_key", "median_score", "p25_score", "p75_score", "n_runs", "device_type"]].copy()
    bench_view["kind"] = bench_view["kind"].astype(str).str.upper()
    bench_view["model_key"] = bench_view["model_key"].map(dashboard.display_name)
    show(
        bench_view.rename(columns={
            "kind": "Kind", "model_key": "Model", "median_score": "Median score",
            "p25_score": "25th pct", "p75_score": "75th pct", "n_runs": "Runs",
            "device_type": "Backend",
        }).round(1),
        paging=True, pageLength=15, order=[[2, "desc"]], showIndex=False,
        classes="display compact",
    )
```
